task_completion.description: The GeoGebra application is open and ready for input.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The GeoGebra window is visible, showing the Algebra View (left) and Graphics View (right).

task_completion.description: The six airport coordinates are entered as points in the Algebra View.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The Algebra View shows six points with coordinates: (-26, 3), (-2, -42), (50, 52), (-36, 53), (11, 3), and (63, 6).

task_completion.description: The Voronoi command is used on the list of airport points.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A Voronoi diagram (a network of cells/lines) is visible in the Graphics View, and the Algebra View shows a 'Voronoi' or 'v1' object created from the list of points.

task_completion.description: A text label 'Service Areas' is added to the diagram.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The text 'Service Areas' is visible on the Graphics View canvas.

task_completion.description: The project is saved with the specific filename in the correct directory.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The GeoGebra title bar or a 'Save As' dialog shows the filename 'london_airports_voronoi.ggb' and the path '~/Documents/GeoGebra/projects/'.

integrity.description: The agent used the GeoGebra GUI to create the diagram rather than just manipulating files via terminal.
integrity.visual_evidence: Screenshots show the mouse cursor interacting with the GeoGebra input bar, tools, or menu items.

integrity.description: The Voronoi diagram is generated from the points, not a static image or manual line drawing.
integrity.visual_evidence: The Algebra View shows the Voronoi object linked to the list of points, and the lines align mathematically with the perpendicular bisectors of the points.

integrity.description: The agent did not simply open an existing .ggb file provided in the environment.
integrity.visual_evidence: The trajectory shows the step-by-step input of coordinates or the creation of the point list.

privileged_info_for_vlm: The six airport coordinates are: Heathrow (-26, 3), Gatwick (-2, -42), Stansted (50, 52), Luton (-36, 53), London City (11, 3), and Southend (63, 6). The Voronoi diagram must be calculated from these specific points. The required text label is 'Service Areas' (case sensitive). The final file must be named 'london_airports_voronoi.ggb' and saved in '~/Documents/GeoGebra/projects/'.
